# Throgg the Troll King

*Pages PDF 38-39*

SEA OF CL AWS 

## **Throgg the Troll King**
**Motivation:** Conquer the south. **Short-Term Ambition:** Muster an army of monsters. **Long-Term Ambition:** Raid Kraka Ravnsvake. 

To name oneself Troll King and withstand the attention of one’s peers is a challenge indeed, but Throgg does so with ease.  All Trolls are prone to mutations, but Throgg’s make him a brute even by Troll standards. He is so huge, one would almost think him kin to Giants. Wielding a stone hammer whose handle was fashioned from a tree trunk, Throgg sweeps aside the mightiest of adversaries. More remarkably, Throgg is possessed of a most unusual mind: while Trolls are typically dull, simple monsters, Throgg is cunning and intelligent. He and his followers hunt and raid, bursting without warning from icy blizzards, slaughtering whole tribes before they can react. 

So go the campfire stories and rumours, which have spread as far as Erengrad and Praag, and even beyond. The tales of his lair are equally fanciful. The truth is, the Human inhabitants of Troll Country and the Norse Dwarfs of Kraka Ravnsvake are uncertain as to the legitimacy of any of these stories. 

However, in recent times scouts and travellers have seen unusual numbers of Trolls in groups travelling towards the region where Throgg is said to lair. Similarly, hunters report a decrease in game in north-eastern Troll country, perhaps because of an increasing number of predatory beasts and more unusual creatures in the area. Even Hell Pit Skaven, foraging for warpstone and captives in the Sturen Ridge, report incidents of disobedient war beasts charging off into northern Troll Country, never to be seen again. 

While northern Troll County is far from civilisation, Kislevite and Imperial strategists take rumours like these very seriously. It would not be the first time a powerful 

_“Sit and talk then, scion of the warm southern lands. It has been some time since I enjoyed a good conversation. But keep a respectful tongue in your head, for I am a king. And if that does not sway you, think on this — it has also been some time since I last ate.”_ 

leader arose in the far north to bring death and destruction to lands much further south. What these strategists need is reliable, first-hand observation and facts. They need someone to go deep into Troll Country, discover the truth behind the rumours, and bring it back. 

The truth is alarming. Where once Throgg was content with a simple life, using his cunning and strategy to achieve simple aims, he has become ambitious. Why should he simply hide in the snows of the north, when the south lies there for the taking? His fellow Trolls seem instinctively drawn to him, despite their usual tendencies. He can call and command beasts, both natural and Chaotic, and bind them to his will. Throgg knows that Troll Country has the potential to provide him with an army, perhaps the greatest assemblage of beasts and monsters ever seen. 

Throgg does not intend to immediately head south, but first plans to attack the Norse Dwarf hold of Kraka Ravnsvake. This is partly to test his troops, but more importantly he doesn’t want Dwarfs at his back when he takes his army south. He is beginning subtly, by destabilising their protective system of runestones. 

Throgg’s drive and ambition are born of frustration. He is a king, but rules alone and without ceremony, holding no court beyond the beasts and brainless Trolls who stalk his lair. His kin lack the wits for conversation or original thought, and Throgg has no one with whom to share his ideas. Brooding on his plans and thinking of a future Empire of Monsters distracts him from his isolation. Perhaps his most unusual scheme is to breed a more intelligent Troll. Rumours of his lair containing kidnapped wizards are indeed true: currently an Imperial wizard, two Sarl vitki, and a Skaven Master Moulder struggle together in this endeavour. 

For those unfortunate enough to meet Throgg, the key to survival is intelligent conversation, something he has precious little experience of. Unsurprisingly, he’s smart enough to know that Humans will use talk to stall for time, but such is his need to express himself that it’s difficult for him to resist it. 

As long as there is no pressing need to kill interlopers, he may take advantage of their company, making them unwilling guests. Can he be persuaded to alter or redirect his goals through reasoned argument? Unlikely, but Throgg would embrace the debate.

## Throgg’s Fishing Trip
Throgg is a keen fisherman, often sitting alone on a cliff or bank, thinking deep thoughts. When he sees a boat, he hurls his viciously hooked line out and attempts to snag it. He then tries to pull the vessel to shore, or simply secures the line and wades out to batter his catch senseless. 

## **Throgg’s Treasures**
**The Wintertooth Crown:** Spat out by Throgg while chewing some once-mighty prince or warrior, this ancient crown possesses considerable magic. Perhaps wrought by Elf craft or blessed by Taal, it draws wild animals to the wearer. _Effects: wearer gains Animal Care +20, Animal Training +30; the Animal Friend Petty Magic spell is always in effect while the crown is worn (Throgg’s Monstrous Size means that even Enormous animals are friendly toward him)._ 

**Throgg’s Maul:** This weapon, with a massive stone head and a handle made from a tree trunk, is unwieldable by creatures with less than Strength 80. However, military engineers could use it to build a powerful battering ram (Reach. Long; Dam. SB+12), causing Fear 2 in defenders. See **Archives of the Empire vol 2** page 88 for more on Battering Rams. 

**Throgg’s Vomit:** Throgg’s vomit is copious, and likely to contain something useful, valuable, or hinting at a subplot. Whenever he vomits, the resulting mess counts as a Bile Pool as described on page 35.
